title: High-ozone days gave more three-day runs than fixed-count random order near selected US bird surveys in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested the order of high-ozone days in 1,120 complete exposure windows before selected bird surveys in four US states in 2005-2019. We compared observed overlapping three-day runs above 70 ppb with exact expectations from random date order at fixed high-day counts. Observed counts were 2.14-15.54 times the 30-day expectations in two regions and two periods. They were 1.37-3.19 times expectations when counts were fixed within five-day blocks. The excess stayed positive with second sites, complete paired sites, equal site weights, and one window per site-year. No single site or year deletion removed the excess. The later eastern sample had only three runs. At 80 ppb, both eastern main samples had no runs. Selected windows covered 20-39% of filtered surveys and had warmer survey starts. These are finite-sample exposure results. Repeated dates, selected monitors, rare events, and assumed random-order references limit inference. We do not estimate weather causes or bird effects. The package gives daily data, exact calculations, source hashes, all checks, and code.

display.caption: Observed three-day runs and exact random-order expectations per 100 complete windows. The left reference fixes the 30-day high-day count. The right reference fixes counts in six five-day blocks. Runs overlap and windows can share monitor dates. Bars do not show independent events or causal effects.

citations.reason: Reuse verified daily ozone evidence, survey window panel, source records and raw-build code. This is a dependent follow-up, not a new biological sample.
Prior paired-site episode-date audit used overlapping source data. We add fixed-count random-order expectations, not another site agreement test.
Prior work on weather persistence and ozone motivates a timing audit. We do not test its meteorological mechanisms.
